payload.rationale: No current evidence was supplied, so this rests on base rates and structural reasoning. Historically the FOMC leaves the policy rate unchanged at roughly 60-70% of scheduled meetings, and the contract also resolves YES if the meeting is canceled, slightly boosting the hold bucket. Countervailing factors: by late 2026 the Fed is plausibly still in an easing cycle (cuts began in late 2025), a new chair appointed in 2026 under strong political pressure for lower rates may favor continued cuts, and December meetings (with fresh projections) are frequent venues for policy moves. Offsetting this, if the funds rate has already drifted toward estimates of neutral by late 2026, the committee is more likely to pause, and any inflation re-acceleration from tariffs or fiscal policy would argue for holding rather than cutting. Hikes look unlikely but not impossible. Netting these, I place the hold probability modestly above 50%. Too high: a dovish new chair and softening labor market could produce a steady sequence of cuts through year-end, making December another cut. Too low: if the Fed has already reached its terminal rate or paused mid-2026, holds become the default at ~70%+; the cancellation clause adds a small extra YES path. The central limitation is having no data on the actual policy path, economic conditions, or FOMC communications as of September 2026.
limitations: No supplied research or current data on 2026 policy path, inflation, or labor market
Unknown composition and stance of the FOMC and new chair in late 2026
Estimate relies on historical hold frequencies rather than meeting-specific signals
Cannot verify whether the December 9, 2026 meeting is scheduled as assumed
